title: Pantone (PMS) Color Matching for Packaging: C vs. U & Drawdowns
seoTitle: Pantone PMS Color Matching for Packaging | MTT
summary: Specify Pantone (PMS) spot colors for custom boxes: Coated (C) vs. Uncoated (U) ink shift, Hex-to-PMS conversion, matte lamination shift, and press drawdowns.
intro: Always specify Pantone Matching System (PMS) solid spot codes with the exact substrate suffix—Coated (C) for laminated art paper or SBS cartons, and Uncoated (U) for raw dyed specialty paper or kraft board—rather than sending RGB Hex codes alone. Screen Hex values convert poorly into CMYK process builds on dark, pastel, or metallic brand tones, and matte BOPP lamination slightly darkens and desaturates printed ink. Approve a physical ink drawdown or wet press proof on your actual production stock before mass printing 1,000+ boxes.
faq: Why does the same Pantone number look different on coated vs. uncoated box paper?
Uncoated and kraft papers absorb ink deeper into porous fibers, making Pantone U inks appear darker, warmer, and slightly muted compared to the same ink resting on clay-coated C1S art paper.
Can I send a website Hex code instead of a Pantone code for box printing?

Hex codes define backlit RGB screen pixels, not physical printing inks. Convert your Hex target to the closest physical Pantone Solid Coated (C) or Uncoated (U) swatch book reference, then confirm the match on a physical proof.
Does matte lamination change my Pantone brand color?
Yes. Matte and soft-touch BOPP films scatter surface light, typically making dark blues, greens, and blacks appear slightly deeper and softer while muting bright saturated reds or oranges.
cta: Share your Pantone C/U codes, target box substrate (coated art paper, dyed specialty stock, or kraft), lamination preference, quantity per design, and destination for a print-proofing review. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, samples, and other fees.
sections: Compare Pantone C, Pantone U, and 4-color CMYK

Brand guidelines often list a single RGB Hex value or one Pantone code across a whole product line. In physical packaging production, paper coating and protective film change how light reflects off the ink film. Use this reference when specifying folding cartons, rigid box wraps, and matching retail bags.

Pantone Solid Uncoated (U)Uncoated dyed specialty stock, white kraftConsistent within same paper mill lotPorous fibers absorb ink; dries flatter than C

Matching one brand color across boxes, bags, and inserts

When a fragrance launch pairs a laminated rigid gift box with an uncoated cotton-cord paper bag and a kraft corrugated shipper, identical ink formulas will not look identical under retail lighting. Specify separate C and U Pantone targets for each substrate, or request a single-lot physical ink drawdown on the actual wrap stock. Review broader print selection rules in our offset vs. digital vs. flexo printing guide and CMYK vs. spot color case.
Pre-press proof checks before releasing 1,000+ units

Digital inkjet proofs simulate CMYK well but cannot reproduce true metallic Pantone 871C/877C gold/silver inks or soft-touch film darkening. For flagship SKUs, approve a wet press sample on the exact production board with final lamination applied, and record the approved Pantone swatch plus delta-E lighting standard (D50 viewing booth) in your specification sheet alongside our custom foil-stamped folding carton and reorder control checklist.

title: Rigid Drawer Boxes: Ribbon Pull vs. Thumb Notch & Slide Fit
seoTitle: Rigid Drawer Box: Ribbon Pull vs. Thumb Notch | MTT
summary: Compare ribbon pull tabs vs. die-cut thumb notches on rigid drawer boxes: pull-force limits, 1.0–1.5 mm sleeve clearance, ribbon heat-sealing, and sleeve sag.
intro: Choose a die-cut semi-circular thumb notch on rigid drawer boxes when you want zero-plastic mono-material recycling, clean flush edges, and fast automated packing; choose a grosgrain or satin ribbon pull tab when a luxury unboxing reveal matters and the drawer carries heavier glass bottles up to roughly 1.2 kg. Keep 1.0–1.5 mm total width and height clearance between the wrapped inner tray and outer rigid sleeve so the drawer glides smoothly without binding under sea-freight humidity.
faq: How much clearance should a rigid drawer box have between the tray and sleeve?

Plan 1.0–1.5 mm total clearance across width and height after wrapping paper and lamination thickness are added. Less than 0.6 mm binds when humid air swells greyboard; more than 2.5 mm lets the tray tip and rattle.
Do ribbon pull tabs tear out on heavy glass gift sets?

Glue-only ribbon tabs can peel if a buyer yanks a heavy 1 kg+ drawer. Anchor the ribbon through a punched slot in the front greyboard wall and trap the tail behind the glued inner liner paper so pull force distributes across the board.
How do factories prevent satin or grosgrain ribbon pulls from fraying?
Production lines cut ribbon pulls with a heated thermal knife (hot-cut) rather than cold shears, fusing polyester fibers cleanly at the cut tip so threads do not unravel during retail handling.
cta: Send your product dimensions, filled tray weight, preferred pull style (thumb notch vs. ribbon pull), quantity per design, and destination for a drawer-fit engineering review. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, samples, and other fees.
sections: Compare ribbon pull tabs vs. die-cut thumb notches

The opening mechanism on a rigid slide-out drawer box affects both perceived luxury and assembly durability. Compare the three standard pull constructions before finalizing your dieline on custom rigid boxes.

Preventing outer sleeve sag and tray binding

Wide drawer boxes over 220 mm span often bow slightly across the top panel of the outer sleeve when stacked inside export cartons, pinching the inner tray. Use 1,200 gsm greyboard for the outer sleeve (with grain running along the longest panel) and 1,000 gsm for the inner tray, paired with a balanced inner liner paper to counteract glue warp. Review loaded sample checks in our drawer clearance checklist and greyboard V-groove guide.
Testing loaded slide resistance before mass production

Never approve drawer slide friction on an empty white dummy: heavy glass jars or tight EVA foam inserts flex tray sidewalls outward by 0.5–1.0 mm, turning a smooth empty slide into a jammed retail box. Test a fully loaded sample through 20 open-close cycles and compare drawer formats on our travel fragrance trio drawer box.

title: Collapsible Fold-Flat Rigid Boxes: CBM Freight & Corner Tape
seoTitle: Fold-Flat Rigid Boxes: CBM Freight & Tape | MTT
summary: Compare fold-flat collapsible vs. assembled rigid boxes: ocean/air CBM freight math, 3M corner tape vs. magnets, and warehouse assembly time.
intro: A collapsible fold-flat rigid box ships flat at roughly one-quarter to one-third the cubic meter (CBM) volume of a pre-assembled rigid box of identical internal size, cutting ocean LCL and air-courier volumetric freight substantially on orders of 1,000+ units. In return, you add roughly 8–15 seconds of manual erection labor at your destination warehouse and must specify reliable corner locking—either peel-and-stick high-tack adhesive triangles or concealed corner magnets—plus creased hinge durability tested across repeated folds.
faq: How much shipping volume does a fold-flat rigid box save compared to assembled boxes?

Exact savings depend on box height: a tall 100 mm deep rigid box folded flat to ~18 mm thickness ships in roughly 70–80% less carton volume, whereas a shallow 35 mm box saves much less and may not justify the extra folding hinge cost.
Which corner closure is better on collapsible boxes: peel-and-stick tape or magnets?

Peel-and-stick double-sided adhesive triangles (such as 3M-grade acrylic tape) lock corners permanently and cost less per unit; concealed corner magnets allow repeated flattening and re-erection but add hardware cost and weight.
Can a fold-flat rigid box hold a custom EVA foam or paperboard insert?
Yes. Inserts ship separately in nested stacks inside master cartons and drop straight into the erected collapsible box during fulfillment, keeping total shipped CBM compact.
cta: Send your target internal box L x W x H, quantity per design, and destination port or ZIP code to compare assembled vs. fold-flat unit price and total shipped CBM. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, samples, and other fees.

Engineering the hinge wrap and corner adhesive

Collapsible rigid boxes fold along precision-spaced greyboard gaps bridged by 157 gsm laminated art paper or tougher specialty kraft wrap. If the outer paper is uncoated or brittle, repeated folding cracks the spine along the hinge line. Always specify matte BOPP lamination or long-fiber bookcloth/specialty paper on hinged panels, and test corner adhesive release liners so warehouse staff can peel tabs cleanly in one motion. Check our collapsible assembly checklist and rigid box freight guide.
When pre-assembled rigid boxes still win

If your box height is under 45 mm, if your co-packer charges high piece-rate assembly fees, or if your design requires razor-sharp V-grooved zero-gap architectural corners, a standard pre-assembled V-grooved magnetic rigid box often delivers lower total landed cost and cleaner corner seams. Compare both structures in your initial RFQ brief.

imageAlt: Four-flap RSC corrugated export shipping carton sized for palletized retail gift boxes
title: Master Shipping Carton Sizes: Packout, Pallet Fit & ECT Stacking
seoTitle: Shipping Carton Sizes: Packout & Pallet Fit | MTT
summary: Size export master shipping cartons for retail gift boxes: 15–20 kg weight limits, 32/44 ECT vs. BC double-wall stacking, and EU/US pallet fit.
intro: Size export master shipping cartons from the outside dimensions of your packed inner gift boxes plus 5–10 mm cushioning clearance per axis, while capping gross carton weight around 15–20 kg so warehouse handlers do not drop oversized boxes. Match outer board grade to transit humidity and pallet height—32 ECT single-wall for lightweight retail cartons, 44 ECT B/C-flute or BC double-wall (6–7 mm) for heavy glass fragrance or skincare shipments—and align outer dimensions to standard 1200 × 1000 mm (US/UK) or 1200 × 800 mm (EU) pallets.
faq: What is the maximum recommended weight for an export master shipping carton?

Keep filled master cartons between 12 and 20 kg (under 22.7 kg / 50 lb for standard US/EU parcel and FBA receiving rules). Cartons over 20 kg suffer far higher corner-drop impact damage during manual loading.
Should I use single-wall or BC double-wall corrugated cartons for glass bottles?

Use 5-ply BC double-wall corrugated board (approx. 6.0–7.0 mm thick) for sea freight carrying heavy glass perfume, candle, or skincare rigid boxes, because container humidity reduces corrugated stacking strength over multi-week voyages.
How much clearance should I leave between retail gift boxes and the master carton wall?
Leave 3–5 mm snug tolerance when using a rigid corrugated inner liner or honeycomb pad, or 10–15 mm if wrapping each rigid gift box in bubble film or tissue plus corner protectors.
cta: Share your individual gift box external dimensions, filled unit weight, order quantity, and destination warehouse rules (FBA, retail DC, or sea pallet) for a master-carton packout calculation. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, samples, and other fees.

Align carton footprint to US and EU pallets

Carton dimensions that overhang a 1200 × 1000 mm (GMA) or 1200 × 800 mm (Euro) pallet lose up to a third of their vertical corner compression strength and get crushed by forklift clamps. Aim for an even column-stacking layout (for example, 400 × 300 mm or 600 × 400 mm outer footprints) with zero overhang, and verify whether your inner boxes require individual polybags or corrugated dividers inside the shipper. Pair outer carton sizing with our rigid gift box outer carton guide and flute & ECT guide.
Preventing finish scuffing inside export shippers

Even when a master carton survives drop tests intact, loose inner rigid boxes rub against rough kraft liners and burnish matte black lamination. Specify snug inner fit, protective tissue or poly-sleeve wrapping per gift box, and top/bottom corrugated pad sheets so box cutters never slice into retail lids during receiving. See also our custom litho-laminated corrugated mailer for direct-to-consumer parcel packs.

imageAlt: Custom luxury paper retail bag with knotted cotton cord handles and reinforced top turnover
title: Custom Paper Bag Handles: Cotton Cord, Ribbon & Load Limits
seoTitle: Paper Bag Handles: Cotton Cord & Ribbon Guide | MTT
summary: Compare custom paper bag handles: 5–6 mm cotton cord, grosgrain ribbon, twisted kraft paper, and die-cut slots by carry load, cost, and recyclability.
intro: Choose 5–6 mm knotted cotton cord or 15–20 mm grosgrain ribbon handles anchored through a 450 gsm reinforced turnover top when your luxury paper bag carries heavy rigid fragrance, wine, or skincare boxes (typically 1.5–3.5 kg). Choose twisted kraft paper handles when 100% mono-material curbside recyclability and lower unit cost outweigh boutique softness, and reserve die-cut hand slots for lightweight apparel or flat gift boxes under 1.0 kg. Always load-test handle knots and bottom seams with filled product samples before mass production.
faq: Which paper bag handle is strongest for heavy glass bottles or wine boxes?

5–6 mm braided cotton or PP cord knotted through metal eyelets (or glued-in wide cotton twill tape) anchored across a 450 gsm turnover top board provides the highest tear resistance for heavy glass sets.
Are knotted cotton or ribbon handles recyclable with the paper bag?
Textile cords and polyester ribbons must be pulled out before paper repulping, whereas twisted paper handles glued with paper patches allow 100% mono-material paper recycling without disassembly.
What is the difference between knotted ribbon handles and glued-in ribbon handles?

Knotted handles pass through punched holes with visible knots inside the bag; glued-in (J-cut or sandwiched) ribbon handles hide the handle tails neatly inside the folded turnover top for a cleaner luxury interior.
cta: Share your inner box dimensions, filled bag weight, preferred handle style (cotton cord, ribbon, or twisted paper), quantity per design, and destination for a bag load and specification review. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, samples, and other fees.
sections: Compare the four custom retail paper bag handles

Sizing handle drop length and turnover depth

Standard hand-carry cotton cords use a 35–40 cm cut length (approx. 13–15 cm drop height above the bag mouth), while shoulder-carry apparel totes need 55–65 cm cords so the bag clears a winter coat sleeve. Pair our custom cotton-cord luxury retail paper bag with a 40–45 mm top turnover board and a 450 gsm bottom insert card so point loads never pull the gusset seam apart.
Checking color match and carry comfort on samples

Dyed cotton cords and grosgrain ribbons come in stock color cards unless ordered in large dye-lot volumes. Approve physical cord swatches beside your laminated bag sheet under retail lighting, and hang a loaded sample with real filled boxes for 24 hours to verify zero hole tearing. Review full bag sizing rules in our Euro tote GSM and gusset guide and paper bag load checklist.

title: How deep should a box be for a sleeved print edition?
seoTitle: How deep should a box be for a sleeved print edition? | MTT
summary: Size the cavity from the complete sleeved edition, including folded seams, mats and the certificate packet. Measure the loaded corners before sample approval.
intro: Size the cavity from the complete sleeved edition, including folded seams, mats and the certificate packet. A stack measured at its centre can understate the height along one edge. Send both measurements and a representative packed set before approving a rigid portfolio box.
faq: Can I size the box by multiplying paper thickness by print count?
Use that calculation for a first estimate. Folded sleeve edges, mounts and the certificate wallet contribute to the assembled depth, so measure a packed dummy before tooling.
cta: Send the packed dimensions, edition size, quantity per design and delivery destination. Custom projects start at 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 in product value per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees.
sections: Measure the loaded corners

Lay the edition on a flat support in pack order. Measure the four corners and centre with the stack resting naturally. If one side rises where sleeve seams align, try alternating seam orientation only if the packing team can repeat it reliably. Record the orientation on the assembly sheet.
Quote the shortest and deepest editions

For an illustrative 12-print set, removing six prints can leave the top half of the cavity empty. Compare separate box depths with one common shell and a removable false bottom. The common shell simplifies artwork but adds a component that can be omitted at packing.
Approve the closure with a dummy edition

Use sacrificial sheets in the production sleeves, then close and reopen the case. Look for a polished line where the lid rubbed the top sleeve, compressed mat corners or a lid sitting proud. Record the accepted stack height and revise the cavity if any contact persists.
What to send for a sample

Include the stack measurements and sleeve seam layout. Review the matted print edition portfolio box with the packing team. For background on protective enclosures and handling, see the Library of Congress collection care guidance. The prototype checks above are proposed purchasing checks.

title: Should a photographic print box use sleeves or folders?
seoTitle: Should a photographic print box use sleeves or folders? | MTT
summary: Choose the primary enclosure from the photographic process and how often the buyer will view the print. Start with the printing studio before sample approval.
intro: Choose the primary enclosure from the photographic process and how often the buyer will view the print. Then design the presentation box around that enclosure. Ask for documentation for the exact contact material before using photo-safe language in a purchase order or on a retail label.
faq: Does a photo-safe sleeve make the whole box archival?
A sleeve supplier can document its own material. Assess the intended storage conditions and every component relevant to the claim before printing it on the box.
cta: Send the packed dimensions, edition size, quantity per design and delivery destination. Custom projects start at 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 in product value per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees.
sections: Start with the printing studio

Identify the image process, finish and storage conditions. A folder lets a print rest on a support while the buyer opens the cover. A transparent sleeve allows inspection through the material, but inserting a vulnerable surface can involve friction. Test the loading movement with a spare from the same print run.
Separate the two supplier decisions

Request a supplier reference and relevant photographic activity test documentation for the enclosure. Record paper, adhesive and lining separately. Evidence for a sleeve cannot establish the performance of a decorative box, and a description such as acid-free leaves other material questions open.
Write a useful acceptance note

Ask the packer to identify the side that opens, the surface that can be touched and the orientation of the image. Have a second person pack and retrieve a dummy using only that note. If they must grip the printed face, change access before selecting decoration.
What to send for a sample

Include the identified print process and enclosure supplier reference. Review the matted print edition portfolio box with the packing team. title: How do I keep print corners clear of a flat mailer closure?
seoTitle: How do I keep print corners clear of a flat mailer closure? | MTT
summary: Build the shipping sample around the finished sleeve and backing sheet. Draw the swept path before sample approval.
intro: Build the shipping sample around the finished sleeve and backing sheet. Position folded stops outside the artwork footprint, then trace where the locking tabs travel during closing. An empty mailer can shut cleanly while a loaded one drives a tab into the corner of an edition.
faq: What should I photograph after a parcel trial?
Take the same corner and surface views before packing and after opening. Include the flap position and the stiffeners so that the packer can locate the source of any mark.
cta: Send the packed dimensions, edition size, quantity per design and delivery destination. Custom projects start at 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 in product value per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees.
sections: Draw the swept path

Use a pencil on a dummy backing sheet to mark the area occupied by each tab as the lid turns. Check the tallest packed version. Move a stop, change flap depth or increase the panel margin if the path overlaps the sleeve. Increasing the entire mailer also changes parcel dimensions.
Test two different failures

An edge stop can prevent sliding yet leave the middle free to bow. Compare a loaded prototype with one using a second stiffener. Support each as it will be handled and inspect the dummy for a crease or compressed edge. Extra board may increase packed weight; weigh both versions before choosing.
Agree what the receiver will inspect

Photograph the dummy corners before the trial. After a representative delivery, open the mailer in order and record external dents separately from shifted stiffeners, sleeve scuffs and bent corners. A single trial helps compare designs but does not establish a shipping damage rate.
What to send for a sample

Include the folded tab drawing and destination. Review the flat mailer for sleeved art prints with the packing team. For background on protective enclosures and handling, see the Library of Congress collection care guidance. The prototype checks above are proposed purchasing checks.

title: How can a customer lift a matted print from a shallow box?
seoTitle: How can a customer lift a matted print from a shallow box? | MTT
summary: Give the buyer a way to lift a support under the mat. Follow the first and last lift before sample approval.
intro: Give the buyer a way to lift a support under the mat. Fingers reaching into a close cavity can press its bevel or touch the image. Compare edge access, a lift-out carrier and a tab on the carrier using the smallest and largest mounts in the edition.
faq: Should the ribbon go directly under a loose print?
Prototype a pull attached to the backing carrier so the carrier takes the load. Check the final sheet as well as the full set.
cta: Send the packed dimensions, edition size, quantity per design and delivery destination. Custom projects start at 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 in product value per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees.
sections: Follow the first and last lift

Load the full set and observe where the hand goes first. Repeat with only the last mat left. A shallow notch may work at the top of a full stack yet leave the final sheet beyond reach. A carrier spanning the base gives the final mat support during removal.
Choose where to attach the tab

Attach a prototype pull to the backing carrier, away from the image and bevel. A central pull can tip a wide mat; two broad grip positions can keep it level but require two hands. Ask whether the intended user opens the box on a counter or holds it during presentation.
Check the return movement

Have a new tester put the mat back without instructions. Look for bent corners, a tab trapped under the backing or a lid that presses a folded tab against the image. Send the accepted grip location and packing sequence with the artwork files.
What to send for a sample

Include the widest mat and intended grip position. Review the matted print edition portfolio box with the packing team. For background on protective enclosures and handling, see the Library of Congress collection care guidance. The prototype checks above are proposed purchasing checks.

title: Where should the certificate go in a numbered print box?
seoTitle: Where should the certificate go in a numbered print box? | MTT
summary: Specify how the packer matches each edition number before choosing a certificate pocket. Match numbers before closing the box before sample approval.
intro: Specify how the packer matches each edition number before choosing a certificate pocket. A lid pocket makes the document easy to find, while a separate wallet can travel with a framed print. Prototype both with the actual certificate, signature position and loaded box.
faq: Can the same pocket hold different editions?
Try each certificate size and signature position. A common pocket works only if a receiver can read and remove every version without catching the corners.
cta: Send the packed dimensions, edition size, quantity per design and delivery destination. Custom projects start at 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 in product value per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees.
sections: Match numbers before closing the box

Set one print and one certificate at the station. Compare identifiers, record the pair and move the complete pair together. If a sheet needs replacement, hold its partner with it until the studio resolves the number. Use dummy identifiers for the first packaging trial.
Place the pocket around the signature

Check whether a thumb cut exposes the signature, whether the card can escape when the lid opens and whether its corners project into the stack. A wallet costs an extra packing step but can accompany the buyer independently. Ask the studio which item the recipient will keep with the framed work.
Run a deliberate mismatch

Give a trial packer two dummy sets with adjacent numbers and switch the certificates. Observe whether the written procedure catches the switch before sealing. Then reopen one completed box: the number should be legible without lifting the print or pulling against the signed face.
What to send for a sample

Include the certificate dimensions and packing sequence. Review the matted print edition portfolio box with the packing team. For background on protective enclosures and handling, see the Library of Congress collection care guidance. The prototype checks above are proposed purchasing checks.
